title: What to watch at the open
text: Markets open soon on Friday. The prices on this board are still Thursday's close: the S&P 500 fund SPY at $769.36 and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ at $715.34. Watch two things at the open. First, Amazon, which reported after the close and has not traded on the news yet. Second, whether Alphabet steadies after its 12.6% fall to $283.82. This is for learning, not advice.

title: Amazon reports a record profit margin
text: After the close on Thursday, Amazon said its sales were $201.9 billion and its operating profit was $28.1 billion, about 13.9% of sales, its best share ever. AWS, its cloud business, grew 39%, the fastest in nearly five years. The stock closed at $243.79, down 4.2%, before the report, so the first trades on Friday will show how investors feel.

title: Alphabet sits near its 52 week low
text: Alphabet closed at $283.82 after a 12.6% drop. That is 30.5% below its 52 week high of $408.61 and only 4.8% above its low of $270.70. Analysts still average a target of $406.41, but a target is only an opinion, and it can change fast after a big move.

title: Eli Lilly is close to its yearly high
text: Eli Lilly jumped 6.6% on Thursday to $1,373, just 2.5% under its 52 week high of $1,408.38. Its beta is only 0.45, which means it usually moves less than the market, so a jump this big is unusual. Big jumps can reverse, so watch whether the price holds.

title: The 10 year Treasury yield is at a one year high
text: The average 10 year Treasury yield in September was 4.99%, up from 4.06% a year earlier. Higher yields make safe bonds more attractive, which can pull money away from stocks, especially fast growing tech companies. AI giants fell 3.8% on average Thursday, while the AI chip and equipment group fell 1.1%.

title: Lesson 30: What is a market index?
text: A market index is a list of companies used as a scoreboard for the market. The S&P 500 follows 500 large US companies. The Nasdaq 100 follows 100 big companies listed on the Nasdaq, many of them tech. Think of it like a class average: it tells you how the group is doing, not how any one student did. Funds like SPY and QQQ copy these lists, so buying one fund gives you a small piece of every company inside. When you hear that the market fell 1%, people usually mean an index like the S&P 500 fell 1%. Some stocks in the index may still have gone up that day, like Eli Lilly on Thursday.
